# Navigation drawer reference

Original Apache-2.0 AndroidX sources are pinned to revision
`a095da93f8e98dea8748ceed79ea8427aade245f`. `sources.json` records URLs and SHA-256
hashes, verified by the browser test before use.

The public API is the reference: permanent/dismissible sheets use Surface,
Rectangle and zero elevation; modal sheets use SurfaceContainerLow, large end
corners and **DrawerDefaults.ModalDrawerElevation = Level0**, despite the unused
token's Level1. NavigationDrawerItem inherits MaterialTheme's BodyLarge because
the public function does not apply the token's LabelLarge text style. Its label,
icon and badge change directly with selection.

`test/browser/navigation-drawer-parity.mjs` checks static geometry, actual rendered
opening/closing bounds, overshoot/counter-scale, scrim fraction, RTL, interruptions,
reduced motion, modal focus, keyboard activation, drag cancellation/thresholds and
reconnect. Independent spring trajectories are generated by tools/androidx-motion.
The pinned DrawerState captures TweenSpec(256) in its AnchoredDraggableState
constructor. Changing anchoredDraggableMotionSpec in SideEffect does not replace
that captured spec. Gesture settlement uses this tween and FastOutSlowIn, or the
default exponential decay (friction -4.2 / speed threshold .1) if its projection
reaches the target. Programmatic open/close use DefaultSpatial/FastEffects.
tools/androidx-drawer compiles unchanged FloatTweenSpec, FloatExponentialDecaySpec,
CubicBezierEasing and Bezier/fastCbrt helpers to export17 independent trajectories.
It also compiles VelocityTracker1D/polyFitLeastSquares unchanged to export15
Lsq2 histories for the pinned flags (minimum-sample fix enabled, Android framework
tracker disabled). The web tracker uses Float QR fitting,20 samples/100ms horizon,
40ms inter-sample limit, excludes UP and clears after a stationary pause over40ms.
Coalesced pointer moves supply historical positions without duplicating the
current point. Pointer cancellation settles to the nearest anchor with zero
velocity, as Draggable.processDragCancel does.

The generator also executes unchanged horizontal TouchSlopDetector and
ViewConfiguration.pointerSlop through84 mouse/touch/stylus cases. Only the
post-slop distance starts moving the drawer; later deltas apply incrementally.
Source startDragImmediately catches a running animation on DOWN, consumes the
event before child presses and stops its RAF. Dragging clamps source overshoot
back to an anchor; captured motion has no fresh slop. Synthetic and real browser
pointer tests verify these behaviors, holding position, small subsequent deltas,
threshold equality and no unintended destination/scrim activation.

Web adaptations: native dialog supplies modal inertness/focus restoration; manual
vertical tab traversal supplies keyboard navigation. Disabled items are an
extension (the source item has no enabled parameter). The web view-configuration
adapter defaults to8CSSpx touch slop and8000CSSpx/s maximum fling velocity; hosts
can configure --md-navigation-drawer-touch-slop and
--md-navigation-drawer-maximum-fling-velocity. These are web inputs, not Material
component tokens. Android obtains them from device ViewConfiguration. Mouse
uses the source .125/18 ratio. Layer touch-action:pan-y lets the browser handle
vertical scrolling. Native event/view-configuration differences and Android
predictive back remain pending. Release tween/decay, slop and default Android Lsq2
velocity math are source-derived and independently checked. Full multi-drawer
gesture ownership, closed-container touch routing and constraint/header edges
remain open.
